In addition to the Main Library, the BA comprises six specialized libraries: the Arts and Multimedia Library, the Taha Hussein Library for the visually impaired, the Children’s Library, the Young People’s Library, the Exchange and Archive Section , and the Rare Books Section . Another library, the Francophone Library, was founded after receiving a massive book donation from the BnF.

International Librarianship Training Program for Arab and non-Arab librarians.

### Conference Center

The Conference Center – Bibliotheca Alexandrina is considered the most renowned convention center in Egypt, Arab region and the Middle East. It garnered its reputation as being the centerpiece of the Bibliotheca Alexandrina.

Read more

### Exhibitions

The BA, with its Arts Center and Art Exhibitions and Collections Department, is a haven for art lovers and a major disseminator of culture in the Egyptian society.

It also houses four major museums: the Sadat Museum (dedicated to the memory of the late President Sadat), the Antiquities Museum, the Manuscripts Museum, and the History of Science Museum.

The Bibliotheca Alexandrina (BA) offers its users an 
extensive collection of electronic resources (free of 
charge) through its subscriptions.
Full access to the electronic resources collection  
is allowed from within Library premises only.
It provides access to numerous full text e-journal  
and e-book titles in addition to a massive number  
of e-theses and dissertations, multimedia resources, 
and more. To access the Library’s electronic resources 
collection, you can do the following: 
In one step, you will be able to 
search the BA electronic and print 
collections through our search facility 
Discover@BA available through our 
website: www.bibalex.org/libraries
• Use the Library computers: Select “electronic 
resources” from the left menu on the internal 
interface.
• Connect to the Library’s WiFi network  
(BA_Public) and access the e-resources collection 
from the Library website:  
www.bibalex.org/libraries
• You can request a list of articles, parts from books 
and theses with respect to the Terms of Use. This 
service is available to students and researchers, 
through the following link: 
https://Tiny.CC/VUM9AY.
• Send your search request to  
Copyright notice:
e-article@bibalex.org (for BA members only).
You will be able to save results retrieved 
from the BA subscribed electronic resources 
by E-mailing and printing with respect to the 
following copyright restrictions:
• All materials retrieved should be used for 
personal, educational, and non-commercial 
purposes ONLY.
• You can save only the following:
−−
One article per issue from an e-journal.
−−
20% of a given e-book and/or e-thesis.

#### [Input] How can I download a book?

Dear Gabriele, 

 

We would like to inform you that book downloading is not available.

Full electronic books can only be accessed from within the library. However, some books whose copyright protection has expired are available for remote access through the following website: http://dar.bibalex.org

 

You are welcome to visit the library to consult other materials on-site. In addition, you may photocopy up to 20% of a book's content in accordance with the library's policies and copyright regulations.

 

 

Best regards,

OPAC Search Advanced

This class familiarizes the patrons with the library's Online Public Access Catalog (OPAC) and different searching techniques. OPAC can be used to search through the library collection by a particular subject, author, title, key words, and more. Patrons will learn three types of searching: Simple, Heading, and Advanced .

At the end of the class, participants will conduct practical training on searching the BA library catalog.

They will also learn how to use the Library of Congress Subject Headings and Shaaban Khalifa Subject Headings.

Prior registration is required at the General Reference Desk at the entrance of the library (E level) or via e-mail to: learning.center@bibalex.org
